Build a "deploy win-back" feature for Nxeon (Next.js + TS + Prisma, worker is a long-running node process): a beautiful branded HTML email plus an automated worker sweep that emails signed-in users who ABANDONED the deploy wizard, offering 50% off their first month — behind an OFF-by-default flag so nothing sends until the owner flips it on.

Work ONLY in worktree **/opt/nxeon-wt-winback/** (node_modules + .env symlinked to prod). Absolute paths under that dir; never edit /opt/nxeon. `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-winback` for shell. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and fix ALL type errors. Do NOT build the app, deploy, restart services, run prisma migrate/generate/db push, or send any real email. Prefer NO schema change (reuse existing models); if one is unavoidable, edit schema.prisma AND write a plain `.sql` migration file for the owner — do not apply it.

REUSE THE EXISTING EMAIL SYSTEM — do not hand-roll HTML from scratch:
- `lib/email-render.ts` — the branded shell + helpers: `BRAND` (violet `#6f47f5`, panel `#f6f5fd`, ink `#1c1638`, etc.), `wrapEmail(inner,{preheader})` (adds the logo header + footer + unsubscribe), `emailEyebrow`, `emailHeading`, `emailParagraph`, `emailNote`, `emailButton(href,label,accent)`, `emailPanel(inner,accent)`, `emailBanner(inner,accent)`, `emailKeyValue`. USE THESE so the email matches every other Nxeon email and inherits the logo + unsubscribe footer.
- `lib/email-templates.ts` — the `emails` catalog. Templates return `{template, subject, html}` via the `emailSection`-style composer (see `emails.welcome`, `emails.genericNotification`). ADD a new entry, e.g. `emails.deployWinback(a: { name?: string|null; couponCode: string; percentOff: number; expiresLabel: string; deployUrl: string })`.
- `lib/mailer.ts` — `sendMail(opts)`. It already calls `mayDeliverTo` so suppression + opt-out are enforced. Send the win-back as a MARKETING message so opt-outs are honored: use the PRODUCT/marketing `NotifyKind` tier (see `lib/prefs.ts` — pick the marketing kind; `notifyTier`/`isSuppressible` classify it). Read `lib/mailer.ts`'s `sendMail` signature + how other callers pass a built email + `NotifyKind` and follow that exactly.

1) THE BRANDED EMAIL (`emails.deployWinback`):
   Compose it from the shell helpers — beautiful, on-brand, mobile-safe (the shell is table-based). Content (adapt the approved copy):
   - Preheader: "Here's 50% off your first month — and setup just got easier."
   - Warm heading + short paragraph: they started setting up a server and didn't finish; we want to help.
   - A prominent COUPON PANEL (use `emailPanel`, violet accent) showing the code big, e.g. the `couponCode`, with "{percentOff}% off your first month · any plan · valid until {expiresLabel}".
   - A reassurance line that setup is now simpler (we prefill sensible defaults incl. the server name — just keep clicking Continue). This is TRUE (shipped).
   - A violet `emailButton` CTA → `deployUrl` ("Finish setting up your server").
   - A friendly "just reply and a real person will help" line. Keep the unsubscribe footer from the shell (do NOT remove it — it's a marketing email).
   Subject: something inviting and non-spammy, e.g. "A little help finishing your server — {percentOff}% off your first month". No emoji-spam; at most one tasteful emoji.

2) PREVIEW ARTIFACT (so the owner can SEE it): add a tiny standalone script `scripts/preview-deploy-winback.mjs` (or .ts runnable with the repo's tooling) that builds `emails.deployWinback({...sample data, couponCode:"COMEBACK50", percentOff:50, expiresLabel:"Sept 30", deployUrl: APP_URL+"/dashboard/deploy"})` and writes the `.html` to `/opt/nxeon-wt-winback/winback-preview.html`. If `lib/email-render`/`email-templates` are `server-only` and can't be imported from a plain script, note that and instead write the script to import the pure builder in whatever way DOES run (or, worst case, output the HTML string to the file via a small ts runner). The goal: a real rendered `winback-preview.html` on disk I can open. Tell me the exact path.

3) THE AUTOMATED SWEEP (`worker/deploy-winback.ts`, exporting `deployWinbackSweep()`):
   Model it on the existing worker sweeps (`worker/coldemail.ts` `coldEmailSendSweep`, `worker/marketing.ts` `marketingDiscoverySweep`) — same structure, logging, and self-pacing. Logic:
   - FLAG GATE (first line): no-op unless a Setting/env flag is ON — read a `Setting` row key `deploy_winback_enabled` (or env `DEPLOY_WINBACK_ENABLED`), default OFF. When off, return immediately (so deploying the code sends nothing).
   - CANDIDATES: distinct `userId` from `DeployFunnelEvent` where `type='step'` and `createdAt` is OLDER than a COOLDOWN (e.g. 2h — don't email someone mid-session) but NEWER than a MAX_AGE (e.g. 7d — stay timely). EXCLUDE a user if: they have any `DeployFunnelEvent` with `type='complete'` (they finished); they own any `Server` (or any completed order) — existing/converting customers; no email or email not verified; `mayDeliverTo` is false (suppressed/opted-out); OR they were already sent this win-back (dedupe — see below).
   - DEDUPE: use the existing `EmailLog` model (read `prisma/schema.prisma` `model EmailLog` around line 2000 for its fields) — before sending, check no prior win-back log row exists for that user (match on a template tag/kind like `"deploy_winback"`); after sending, WRITE an `EmailLog` row tagged the same so it's once-per-user (or once per, say, 90 days — pick once-per-user for safety and note it). If `EmailLog` can't express a per-user template tag cleanly, that's the only case you may add a minimal dedupe (a boolean/timestamp field on User, or a tiny table) + migration SQL.
   - SEND: build `emails.deployWinback(...)` with the campaign coupon code (a constant `WINBACK_COUPON_CODE = "COMEBACK50"` — the owner will create this coupon), call `sendMail` with the marketing `NotifyKind`, then log to `EmailLog`.
   - SAFETY LIMITS: cap sends per sweep run (e.g. 25) to avoid a burst; self-pace the sweep (run at most every ~15 min via a last-run timestamp like the other sweeps); wrap each send in try/catch so one failure doesn't abort the batch; log counts.
   - REGISTER it in `worker/index.ts` alongside the other sweeps, following the exact pattern used there (import + call in the poll loop with its cadence). It stays inert because the flag defaults OFF.

CONSTRAINTS: reuse email shell + mailer + suppression + EmailLog; marketing NotifyKind so opt-outs/unsubscribe are honored; flag-gated OFF by default; once-per-user dedupe; skip existing customers + completers; tsc clean; no build/deploy/db/email-send. Keep the coupon code in ONE constant.

RETURN (final text = data for me, no preamble): (1) files added/changed, 1 line each; (2) the exact path of the rendered `winback-preview.html`; (3) the candidate/exclusion logic in plain English (cooldown, max-age, all exclusions) and the dedupe mechanism; (4) how compliance is enforced (marketing kind, suppression, unsubscribe footer); (5) EXACTLY how the owner turns it on (the Setting key / env var and its values) and what coupon code it expects; (6) whether any schema/migration was needed (and the .sql path if so); (7) how to test the sweep safely without spamming; (8) risks. Branch wt-winback, commit nothing.

6	 * import TYPES ONLY — the `mayDeliverTo` helper below reaches for `./db`). The
7	 * `"use server"` action file may only export async functions, so all of this
8	 * lives here.
9	 *
10	 * WHY THIS FILE GREW A POLICY (2026-07-26)
11	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
12	 * `User.notificationPrefs` was written by the settings form and read by NOTHING
13	 * (QA-PRELAUNCH P1-32). A customer who unticked "Account email" still received
14	 * every receipt; the "Security alerts" toggle governed a channel that was never
15	 * built. That is the same defect this codebase keeps shipping: a control that
16	 * reports success and is read by nothing — the auto-suspend kill switch an
17	 * operator turned off before watching customer VMs get suspended anyway
18	 * (P1-5), and the domain-markup panel that displayed 0% while charging 25%
19	 * (P1-9).
20	 *
21	 * The dangerous half of fixing it is OVER-fixing it. If a preference could
22	 * suppress a declined payment, an imminent suspension, a security/2FA change or
23	 * a data-loss warning, then an unticked checkbox would silently swallow the one
24	 * message the customer had to see — and they would lose a server, or an
25	 * account, with no warning at all. That is strictly worse than the original bug.
26	 *
27	 * So suppressibility is decided by a message's TIER, declared once in the
28	 * catalogue below, and never by the call site. A send site cannot make itself
29	 * suppressible by passing the wrong flag, and an unrecognised kind resolves to
30	 * CRITICAL — if we guess wrong, we guess towards "delivered".
31	 */
32	
33	export type NotificationPrefs = {
34	  /**
35	   * Non-urgent transactional EMAIL: payment receipts, activity notices.
36	   * Never covers the dunning sequence, suspensions or security changes.
37	   */
38	  email: boolean;
39	  /**
40	   * Product news / marketing. Unticking this also removes the address from the
41	   * campaign list (see `updateNotificationPrefs`) — the stored flag alone would
42	   * suppress nothing, because campaigns are addressed by email, not by user.
43	   */
44	  product: boolean;
45	  /**
46	   * Legacy key, pinned `true`.
47	   *
48	   * It used to render as a "Security alerts" toggle, which was dishonest twice
49	   * over: the channel it claimed to govern was never built (sign-in / token /
50	   * 2FA paths write audit rows only), and security, password and 2FA messages
51	   * must not be suppressible in the first place. Kept in the shape so
52	   * previously-stored values and the GDPR export keep round-tripping, and typed
53	   * as the literal `true` so no code path can ever write it back as
54	   * consent-withdrawn.
55	   */
56	  security: true;
57	};
58	
59	export const DEFAULT_PREFS: NotificationPrefs = { email: true, product: true, security: true };
60	
61	/**
62	 * Normalise whatever is stored in the Json column into a typed prefs object.
63	 * A missing or malformed key falls back to the default (opted IN) — the column
64	 * is nullable and predates this policy, so "absent" must never read as "the
65	 * customer opted out of everything".
66	 */
67	export function normalizePrefs(raw: unknown): NotificationPrefs {
68	  const p = (raw ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
69	  return {
70	    email: typeof p.email === "boolean" ? p.email : DEFAULT_PREFS.email,
71	    product: typeof p.product === "boolean" ? p.product : DEFAULT_PREFS.product,
72	    security: true,
73	  };
74	}
75	
76	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
77	/*                          Delivery policy                                   */
78	/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
79	
80	/** How a message reaches the customer. */
81	export type NotifyChannel = "email" | "inapp";
82	
83	/**
84	 * Suppressibility tier.
85	 *
86	 * CRITICAL — "you need to know this". Delivered on every channel, always,
87	 *            whatever the preferences say. Money that failed to move, a service
88	 *            about to be suspended or deleted, a change to how the account is
89	 *            secured, or anything that can cost the customer data.
90	 * ACCOUNT  — informational transactional. Email is suppressible via
91	 *            `prefs.email`; the in-app bell is kept (see `isSuppressible`).
92	 * PRODUCT  — marketing. Suppressible on every channel via `prefs.product`.
93	 */
94	export type NotifyTier = "CRITICAL" | "ACCOUNT" | "PRODUCT";
95	
96	/**
97	 * Every message kind the platform can send, and the ONE thing that decides
98	 * whether a preference may hold it back. Grouped by tier so the split is
99	 * reviewable at a glance — adding a kind is a deliberate act, and putting
100	 * something in ACCOUNT is a statement that a customer missing it entirely costs
101	 * them nothing they cannot recover.
102	 */
103	export const NOTIFY_KINDS = {
104	  // ---- CRITICAL: never suppressible, on any channel, by any preference. -----
105	  /** Password-reset link. The only way back into a locked-out account. */
106	  password_reset: "CRITICAL",
107	  /**
108	   * Email-verification link. CRITICAL for the same reason as the reset link, not
109	   * because it is urgent: an unverified account cannot buy or provision
110	   * (lib/email-verification.ts), so this message is the ONLY way past that gate.
111	   * Letting a preference suppress it would leave the customer refused at
112	   * checkout with no way to fix it — a locked door whose key we withheld.
113	   */
114	  email_verify: "CRITICAL",
115	  /** Password changed, 2FA enabled/disabled, backup codes reissued, API token created/revoked. */
116	  security_change: "CRITICAL",
117	  /** Card declined, dunning retry declined, final notice. Money did not move. */
118	  payment_failed: "CRITICAL",
119	  /** 3-D Secure / `requires_action` — the payment stalls until the customer acts. */
120	  payment_action_required: "CRITICAL",
121	  /** Saved card expires soon: the next renewal will fail if it is not replaced. */
122	  card_expiring: "CRITICAL",
123	  /** Term is about to lapse. Suppressing this is how a paid-up customer loses a VM. */
124	  expiry_warning: "CRITICAL",
125	  /** Service suspended, or about to be. */
126	  suspension: "CRITICAL",
127	  /** Service terminated, or about to be — data destruction is imminent/done. */
128	  termination: "CRITICAL",
129	  /** Abuse / acceptable-use action against the account. */
130	  abuse: "CRITICAL",
131	  /** Anything that lost, or may lose, customer data (failed backup, restore, volume). */
132	  data_loss: "CRITICAL",
133	  /** Paid but not provisioned — the customer's money is in limbo. */
134	  fulfilment_failed: "CRITICAL",
135	  /** Refund or write-off issued against the account. */
136	  refund: "CRITICAL",
137	
138	  // ---- ACCOUNT: informational transactional. Email opt-out honoured. -------
139	  welcome: "ACCOUNT",
140	  /** Receipt for a payment that SUCCEEDED. (A failure is `payment_failed`.) */
141	  receipt: "ACCOUNT",
142	  invoice: "ACCOUNT",
143	  /** Deploy / reinstall / migration finished successfully. */
144	  provision_done: "ACCOUNT",
145	  /** Backup taken, app installed, certificate issued, volume attached, … */
146	  job_done: "ACCOUNT",
147	  /** Domain registered / renewed / transferred. */
148	  domain_activity: "ACCOUNT",
149	  support_reply: "ACCOUNT",
150	  referral_bonus: "ACCOUNT",
151	
152	  // ---- PRODUCT: marketing. Suppressible everywhere. ------------------------
153	  product_news: "PRODUCT",
154	} as const satisfies Record<string, NotifyTier>;
155	
156	export type NotifyKind = keyof typeof NOTIFY_KINDS;
157	
158	/**
159	 * Tier of a message kind. An unregistered kind resolves to CRITICAL on purpose:
160	 * the failure mode of a mis-typed or forgotten kind must be "delivered anyway",
161	 * never "silently dropped".
162	 */
163	export function notifyTier(kind: NotifyKind): NotifyTier {
164	  return (NOTIFY_KINDS as Record<string, NotifyTier>)[kind] ?? "CRITICAL";
165	}
166	
167	/**
168	 * Does this (kind, channel) pair depend on the customer's preferences at all?
169	 *
170	 * `false` means the answer is unconditionally "deliver", so callers can skip the
171	 * preference lookup entirely — the gate costs nothing on the critical paths.
172	 */
173	export function isSuppressible(kind: NotifyKind, channel: NotifyChannel): boolean {
174	  const tier = notifyTier(kind);
175	  if (tier === "CRITICAL") return false;
176	  if (tier === "ACCOUNT") {
177	    // Email only. The in-app bell is the durable record inside the portal, and
178	    // the toggle the customer ticked says "email" — hiding an activity notice
179	    // from the portal would recreate the very failure this policy exists to
180	    // cure (information that quietly went missing), while suppressing the mail
181	    // is exactly what was asked for.
182	    return channel === "email";
183	  }
184	  return true; // PRODUCT — marketing has no business on a channel they declined.
185	}
186	
187	/** Decide delivery from already-loaded preferences. */
188	export function mayDeliver(
189	  prefs: NotificationPrefs,
190	  kind: NotifyKind,
191	  channel: NotifyChannel,
192	): boolean {
193	  if (!isSuppressible(kind, channel)) return true;
194	  return notifyTier(kind) === "PRODUCT" ? prefs.product : prefs.email;
195	}
196	
197	/**
198	 * Decide delivery for a user id, loading their preferences only when the answer
199	 * actually depends on them.
200	 *
201	 * Fails OPEN. A missing user row or a database hiccup returns `true`: a message
202	 * must never be dropped because a preference lookup failed — that would be a
203	 * silent swallow with no preference behind it at all.
204	 *
205	 * `./db` is imported lazily so this module stays statically safe to import from
206	 * anywhere (the settings page imports `normalizePrefs`, the client component
207	 * imports the type only).
208	 */
209	export async function mayDeliverTo(
210	  userId: string,
211	  kind: NotifyKind,
212	  channel: NotifyChannel,
213	): Promise<boolean> {
214	  if (!isSuppressible(kind, channel)) return true;
215	  try {
216	    const { db } = await import("./db");
217	    const row = await db.user.findUnique({
218	      where: { id: userId },
219	      select: { notificationPrefs: true },
220	    });
221	    if (!row) return true;
222	    return mayDeliver(normalizePrefs(row.notificationPrefs), kind, channel);
223	  } catch {
224	    return true;
225	  }
226	}

253	/**
254	 * Persist one section of settings. Bind the section server-side in the panel
255	 * (`saveSettings.bind(null, "general")`) so it's never client-supplied; React's
256	 * useActionState then supplies (prevState, formData).
257	 */
258	export async function saveSettings(
259	  section: string,
260	  _prev: Result | undefined,
261	  formData: FormData,
262	): Promise<Result> {
263	  const fields = SECTION_FIELDS[section];
264	  if (!fields) return { error: "Unknown settings section." };
265	
266	  const area = BILLING_SECTIONS.has(section) ? "billing" : "platform";
267	  const user = await requireArea(area);
268	
269	  const changes: { key: string; value: string }[] = [];
270	
271	  for (const f of fields) {
272	    const raw = formData.get(f.key);
273	
274	    if (f.type === "bool") {
275	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: raw ? "true" : "false" });
276	      continue;
277	    }
278	
279	    if (f.type === "secret") {
280	      const v = (raw ?? "").toString();
281	      if (v.trim() === "") continue; // never clear/overwrite a stored secret with blank
282	      // Encrypt at rest. `smtp_pass` was the last secret in the DB stored as
283	      // plaintext while mailbox passwords and the Cloudflare token both use the
284	      // AES-256-GCM box. Read-back in lib/mailer.ts decrypts, tolerating a legacy
285	      // plaintext row until it is next saved. Never render — SecretField shows
286	      // only `isSet` — so this closes an at-rest exposure, not a live leak.
287	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: encryptSecret(v) });
288	      continue;
289	    }
290	
291	    if (f.type === "enum") {
292	      const s = (raw ?? "").toString().trim();
293	      if (s === "") {
294	        changes.push({ key: f.key, value: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[f.key as keyof typeof SETTINGS_DEFAULTS] ?? "" });
295	        continue;
296	      }
297	      // A <select> constrains the browser, not the request.
298	      if (!f.values?.includes(s)) {
299	        return { error: `“${f.key}” must be one of: ${f.values?.join(", ")}.` };
300	      }
301	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: s });
302	      continue;
303	    }
304	
305	    if (f.type === "int" || f.type === "num") {
306	      const s = (raw ?? "").toString().trim();
307	      if (s === "") {
308	        changes.push({ key: f.key, value: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[f.key as keyof typeof SETTINGS_DEFAULTS] ?? "0" });
309	        continue;
310	      }
311	      const n = Number(s);
312	      if (!Number.isFinite(n)) return { error: `“${f.key}” must be a number.` };
313	      // Refuse rather than clamp, so the stored row always equals what the operator
314	      // can read back off the field. Silent clamping is how a panel ends up showing
315	      // one number while the platform enforces another.
316	      if (f.min !== undefined && n < f.min) {
317	        return { error: `“${f.key}” must be at least ${f.min} (you entered ${s}).` };
318	      }
319	      if (f.max !== undefined && n > f.max) {
320	        return { error: `“${f.key}” must be ${f.max} or less (you entered ${s}).` };
321	      }
322	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: f.type === "int" ? String(Math.round(n)) : String(n) });
323	      continue;
324	    }
325	
326	    if (f.type === "json") {
327	      // Empty clears back to the default (an empty override → the built-in rate
328	      // table). A non-empty value must parse to a JSON object, so the operator is
329	      // TOLD when they fat-finger it rather than the reader silently ignoring it
330	      // (parseRatesOverride fails safe on read, but a silent no-op in the panel is
331	      // exactly the "shows one thing, does another" trap this file avoids).
332	      const s = (raw ?? "").toString().trim();
333	      if (s === "") {
334	        changes.push({ key: f.key, value: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[f.key as keyof typeof SETTINGS_DEFAULTS] ?? "" });
335	        continue;
336	      }
337	      try {
338	        const parsed = JSON.parse(s);
339	        if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== "object" || Array.isArray(parsed)) {
340	          return { error: `“${f.key}” must be a JSON object, e.g. {"EUR":0.92,"GBP":0.79}.` };
341	        }
342	      } catch {
343	        return { error: `“${f.key}” is not valid JSON.` };
344	      }
345	      changes.push({ key: f.key, value: s });
346	      continue;
347	    }
348	
349	    changes.push({ key: f.key, value: (raw ?? "").toString().trim() });
350	  }
351	
352	  // Cross-field: the dunning schedule must run in the order the panel's own hints
353	  // promise — grace (dunning starts) ≤ warn (final-warning email) < terminate (VM
354	  // destroyed). Field-level bounds cannot catch an inverted schedule, and an
355	  // inverted one deletes a customer's server before, or without, warning them.
356	  // worker/billing.ts also clamps on read; this check exists so the operator is
357	  // TOLD, instead of having their numbers silently rewritten behind the panel.
358	  if (section === "billing") {
359	    const day = (k: string) => Number(changes.find((c) => c.key === k)?.value);
360	    const grace = day("dunning_grace_days");
361	    const warn = day("dunning_warn_days");
362	    const terminate = day("dunning_terminate_days");
363	    if (warn < grace) {
364	      return { error: `Dunning warn (${warn}d) cannot come before dunning grace (${grace}d).` };
365	    }
366	    if (terminate <= warn) {
367	      return { error: `Dunning terminate (${terminate}d) must come after the final warning (${warn}d).` };
368	    }
369	  }
370	
371	  if (changes.length === 0) return { ok: true };
372	
373	  await db.$transaction(
374	    changes.map((c) =>
375	      db.setting.upsert({ where: { key: c.key }, update: { value: c.value }, create: { key: c.key, value: c.value } }),
376	    ),
377	  );
378	
379	  await db.auditLog.create({
380	    data: {
381	      userId: user.id,
382	      action: "settings.save",
383	      detail: `${section}: ${changes.map((c) => c.key).join(", ")}`,
384	    },
385	  });
386	
387	  revalidatePath("/admin/settings");
388	  return { ok: true };
389	}
